To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) human brain mRNA induces ChE activity in Xenopus oocytes; (ii) human brain mRNA produces ‘true’ and ’pseudo’ ChEs in the oocytes; (iii) different size mRNA species induce ‘true’ and 'pseudo' ChEs; (iv) different amounts of mRNA species are found in different human tissues; and (v) different amounts of different size mRNA species are found among different human tissues.
human brain ChEs are encoded by multiple mRNA species, which are translated into distinct molecular forms of ChEs.
human brain mRNA(s) can induce the expression of multiple forms of cholinesterases in Xenopus oocytes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular heterogeneity in the human brain, and the possible implications of this heterogeneity in the pathogenesis of neurodegenerative disorders such as Alzheimer's disease.
the expression and regulation of the cholinesterase (ChE) gene(s) in the human nervous and other tissues.
the identification and molecular characterization of the human brain ChE genes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there exist multiple cholinesterase mRNAs in the human nervous tissue and that the heterogeneity in molecular forms of ChEs is not limited to post‐translatory modifications.
human brain contains at least four different ChE‐inducible mRNAs, and that these are translated into at least four different molecular forms of ChEs.
there are at least two different ChE genes, each of which is expressed in different brain tissues and each of which is translated into at least three molecular forms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the heterogeneity in the substrate specificities and the molecular forms of human nervous system ChEs are due to a combination of post‐translatical and translational mechanisms.
the molecular heterogeneity in ChEs is not limited to a single level but is expressed at the level of mRNA, protein and enzyme activity.
there are at least two types of mRNA species, one for the true cholinesterase (ChE) activity and another for the pseudo‐ChE activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a lot of variation in the size of the mRNA that codes for the enzyme cholinesterase.
there is a diversity of ChE‐encoding transcripts in the human nervous tissues and that this heterogeneity may be a reflection of the complexity of human brain function and disease.
the heterogeneity in the human nervous systems is not limited to post‐translatalion level, but extends up to mRNA level.
